title: Checkout Spec Review
subtitle: Sample board filled with test data from the review-board skill tests. Nothing here is real.

groups.title: Foundations
groups.blurb: Decide these first. Later items depend on them.

groups.title: Payments
groups.blurb: How money moves and what happens when it fails.

groups.title: Wording
groups.blurb: Terms and copy the spec uses inconsistently.

groups.title: Refunds
groups.blurb: Added in round 2 at your request. Start with D1; the others build on it.

items.title: Guest checkout or accounts only?
items.issue: The spec says both "no sign-up required" and "orders are saved to the customer's account".
items.rec: Allow guest checkout, and offer to create an account after payment.

items.title: Which launch markets?
items.issue: Tax, currency and payment methods all depend on the countries served, and the spec names none.
items.rec: Name the launch countries, then revisit sections B and C.

items.title: Add measurable success criteria
items.issue: "Checkout should feel fast" can't be tested.
items.rec: Target: p95 time from Pay to confirmation under 3 seconds, and at most 3 screens.

items.title: What happens when a payment times out?
items.issue: The customer may be charged without seeing a confirmation, then pay again. With PayNow and FPX (B2) the result can also arrive after the customer comes back from their bank app.
items.rec: Show "Checking your payment" for up to 30 seconds. If there's still no result, show an "Order pending" page that updates itself, and email the customer the outcome. Offer a retry only once the payment has definitely failed. Never charge twice for one order.
items.changed: Rewritten after your question: a 30-second wait, then an order-pending page, instead of 60 seconds then a retry.

items.title: Local payment methods
items.issue: Cards alone cover a minority of payments in some launch markets.
items.rec: Support the most-used local method in each launch market from day one.

items.title: How many automatic payment retries?
items.issue: The spec says failed payments are "retried" but not how often, so a card could be charged attempts indefinitely.
items.rec: Retry at most 3 times over 24 hours, then email the customer.

items.title: "Order" and "purchase" are used interchangeably
items.issue: Support staff and the API docs will copy whichever word they see.
items.rec: Use "order" everywhere. Keep "purchase" only for the button label.

items.title: Order confirmation email wording
items.issue: The confirmation email says "Create an account to track this order". Accounts are now required (A1), so every order already belongs to an account.
items.rec: Remove that line, and show "View your order" linking to the order in the customer's account.
items.changed: Rewritten after A1: accounts are required, so there are no guest orders.

items.title: Partial refunds: allowed, and how are they chosen?
items.issue: The spec doesn't cover refunds at all. Support will need to refund part of an order, such as one damaged item out of five.
items.rec: Allow partial refunds by item and quantity, plus a custom amount for goodwill gestures. A refund can never exceed what is left of the amount paid.
items.ref: Not in spec (raised in Anything else?)

options.label: By item and quantity, plus a custom amount

items.title: How is a partial refund's amount worked out?
items.issue: When an order had a discount, shipping or tax (GST in Singapore, SST in Malaysia), refunding one item raises the question of how much of each to give back.
items.rec: Spread order-wide discounts across items in proportion to their price, so each item refunds what was actually paid for it, tax included. Refund shipping only when the whole order is refunded or the mistake was ours.
items.ref: Not in spec (raised in Anything else?)

items.title: Where does refunded money go?
items.issue: Card refunds go back to the card. Depending on the payment provider, PayNow and FPX refunds may not be able to go back the same way automatically.
items.rec: Refund to the original payment method. Where the provider can't, refund by bank transfer to an account the customer confirms, and say so in the refund email.
items.ref: Not in spec (raised in Anything else?)

items.title: Who can issue a refund?
items.issue: The spec doesn't say who can refund an order or whether large refunds need approval.
items.rec: Support staff can refund up to a set limit per order on their own (suggested: S$200, or the RM equivalent); larger refunds need a manager's approval. Every refund records who issued it and why.
items.ref: Not in spec (raised in Anything else?)

items.title: Can customers request a refund from their account?
items.issue: With accounts required (A1), customers could ask for a refund from their order page instead of emailing support.
items.rec: Yes: customers pick the items and a reason on their order page, and support approves or declines it under the rules in D1 to D4.
items.ref: Not in spec (raised in Anything else?)
